e-7580.knowledge_point: Computing the Mean of a Data Set From the Sum
e-7580.problem: Given a data set with $12$ data points and $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{12} x_i = 96,$ compute $\overline{x}.$
e-7580.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n,$ then the mean is denoted by $\overline{x}$ and is given by the following formula:

$$
\overline{x} = \dfrac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n x_i
$$

Substituting $n=12$ and $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{12} x_i = 96,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{12}\cdot 96=8.\end{aligned}
$$

e-7581.knowledge_point: Computing the Mean of a Data Set
e-7581.problem:
What is the mean of the following data set?

$$
9, \: 10, \: 8, \: 11, \: 12
$$
e-7581.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n,$ then the mean is denoted by $\overline{x}$ and is given by the following formula:

$$
\overline{x} = \dfrac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n x_i
$$

Here, there are $n=5$ data points. Adding up all the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{x}_{i} & =9+10+8+11+12 \\  & =50.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot 50 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

e-7582.knowledge_point: Finding Missing Values in a Data Set Given the Mean
e-7582.problem:
Given that the mean of the following data set is $9,$ find the value of $a\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
5, \: 3, \: a, \: a, \: a, \: 7
$$
e-7582.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n,$ then the mean is denoted by $\overline{x}$ and is given by the following formula:

$$
\overline{x} = \dfrac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n x_i
$$

Here, there are $n=6$ data points. Adding up all the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{6}{x}_{i} & =5+3+a+a+a+7 \\  & =15+3a.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mean is given by the expression

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (15+3a) \\  & =\frac{15+3a}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we're told that $\overline{x} = 9,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & =\frac{15+3a}{6} \\ 54 & =15+3a \\ 39 & =3a \\ a & =13.\end{aligned}
$$
